university.name: Thal University Bhakkar
university.tagline: Knowledge for the heart of the Thal.
university.address: Thal University Bhakkar, Bhakkar, Punjab, Pakistan
university.hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:00 pm

history: Thal University Bhakkar was founded to bring higher education to the people of the Thal region, so that students from Bhakkar, Layyah, Mianwali and nearby towns no longer have to leave home to earn a degree.

It began with a handful of departments and has grown to fifteen, with new labs, a central library and hostels for both men and women. Many of our students are the first in their family to attend university.
Today the university works with local schools, farmers, businesses and government offices, and its graduates teach, farm, build software and practise law across South Punjab.
about.vision: To be the leading university of South Punjab, known for honest teaching, useful research and graduates who serve their communities.
about.mission: To offer affordable, good quality education; to carry out research that helps the Thal region; and to build character, discipline and respect for others in every student.

vc.name: Prof. Dr. Muhammad Aslam Khan
vc.title: Vice Chancellor
message: Welcome to Thal University Bhakkar. A university is only as good as the questions it teaches its students to ask, and we want every student here to learn to ask them carefully and answer them honestly.

Our teachers are available, our labs are open, and our doors are open too. I encourage you to use every facility we have and to take part in societies, sports and community work alongside your studies.
We are proud of this region and its people. Come and help us build something that lasts.

installments: Semester fee may be paid in two equal installments.
The first installment is due at the time of admission or re-registration; the second within 45 days of the start of classes.
A late fee of Rs 500 per week applies after the due date, up to a maximum of Rs 3,000.
Students with an unpaid second installment cannot receive their datesheet or admit card.
Installment requests must be submitted to the Finance Office before the first due date.
feeNote: Fees shown for Semesters 1 to 8. Fees for later semesters of five-year programs are announced by the Finance Office. Fees may change; the notified fee on the challan is final.

notes: Vans run Monday to Friday on university working days only.
Students must carry the university card; it is checked at boarding.
Pay the challan at any branch of the named bank before the due date and submit the student copy to the Transport Office.
A late payment fine of Rs 200 applies after the due date.

eligibility.text: Intermediate (FA, FSc, ICS, I.Com or equivalent) with at least 45% marks. Subject requirements vary by department.

16 years of education with at least 2.5 CGPA or 50% marks, plus an interview.

faq.q: Can I apply to more than one department?
faq.a: Yes. You can select up to three departments in order of preference on one form.

faq.q: Is there a quota for students from Bhakkar district?
faq.a: Seats are reserved for local students as per the notified university policy. The exact number is published with every admission advertisement.
For BS, BBA, LLB and Agriculture programs, yes. ADP and master's programs are admitted on merit and, where required, an interview.

faq.q: Can I get a hostel seat along with my admission?
faq.a: Hostel seats are limited and are given after admission on a first-come basis, with priority to students living more than 40 km from the campus.

faq.q: How do I apply for a scholarship?
faq.a: Collect the scholarship form from the Student Affairs Office after admission and submit it with the required documents in the first month.

faq.q: What if I miss the fee deadline?
faq.a: Your seat may go to the next candidate on the merit list. You may request a one-time extension from the Registrar's Office with a valid reason.

exams.intro: Each semester has one mid-term and one final exam. The datesheet is displayed on the notice board and the website at least 15 days before the exams.
rules: Minimum 75% attendance is required to sit the final exam.
Students must bring their university card and admit card.
Mobile phones and smart watches are not allowed in the exam hall.
Results are announced within four weeks of the last paper.
Rechecking applications are accepted within seven days of the result.
Students must carry the university card on campus at all times.
Attendance of at least 75% is required in every course.
Ragging, harassment and discrimination of any kind lead to disciplinary action.
Smoking, drugs and weapons are strictly prohibited on campus.
Students must follow the dress code: modest, clean and appropriate for an educational setting.
Political activity and unauthorised gatherings are not permitted inside the university.
Damage to university property will be charged to the student.
Complaints may be made to the Student Affairs Office or the Discipline Committee.
